alt: Paper 2 Exercise 4 is worth 8 marks: multiple-choice questions on one discussion between two speakers, heard twice. It is the only exercise that assesses all four listening objectives, L1 to L4.
caption: One two-speaker discussion, every listening objective.

alt: A table of Exercise 4 question types with typical Urdu stems: L1 detail (کس دن، کہاں), L2 opinion (کی کیا رائے ہے؟) and objection (اعتراض), L3 connection (دونوں کس بات پر متفق ہوتے ہیں؟), and L4 meaning, feeling (کیسا محسوس کرتا ہے؟) and purpose (اس گفتگو کا مقصد کیا ہے؟).
caption: Read the stem to know whether you need a fact, a view, a link or an implication.

alt: A table of Urdu turn-openers by reaction: full agreement (بالکل ٹھیک), partial agreement (یہ خیال برا نہیں، مگر ...), disagreement (میں ایسا نہیں سمجھتا), hesitation (ہمم، پتا نہیں), surprise (ارے!), admiration (واہ!) and annoyance (اُف!). Partial agreement signals a reservation.
caption: Track who says what: the reply after a suggestion shows the reaction.

alt: A table of feeling words that appear in options, with what a speaker might say instead: پُرجوش (excited), مایوس (disappointed), پریشان (worried), حیران (surprised), متاثر (impressed), مطمئن (satisfied) and ناراض (annoyed). Tone also carries meaning.
caption: The option names the feeling; the speaker only shows it.

after: ## The four kinds of wrong option
alt: Four types of distractor: right words but the wrong speaker, an idea suggested then rejected, a true statement that answers a different question, and a reported view that is then corrected.
caption: Eliminate by type: explain why each other option is wrong.

after: ## A routine for the two hearings
alt: Four stages: in the pause read the stems and note both speakers' initials; on the first hearing mark provisional choices and who said what; on the second confirm, listening to replies and the final lines; then check one answer per question.
caption: Know who said what: initials in the margin, notes on every turn.

alt: A four-line exchange in which Nadia has heard Bilal gave up guitar and Bilal explains his teacher moved away and online classes failed because of slow internet. Question (a) answer B: his teacher moved, while A is the reported view he corrects. Question (b) answer C: online classes were not useful, which is implied.
caption: Reject the reported view and the contradicted option; choose what the speaker means.
